newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: IPC clarifies disposal of overseas units.
newsitem.headline: IPC clarifies disposal of overseas units.

text.p: IPC Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it had completed the disposal of its unprofitable overseas units in December 1996 but had contractually agreed with the buyers on an effective date of January 1, 1996.
In 1996 results released earlier this week, IPC had reported significantly lower sales of S$63.46 million for the second half, compared with sales of S$738.43 million in the first half.
Singapore media reports subsequently raised questions on the timing of the disposal of IPC's unprofitable units and its accounts.

In response, IPC said late on Tuesday that its first half sales were actually S$414.57 million, after adjusting for disposal of unprofitable units on the effective date of January 1. Second half sales were therefore S$387.33 million, it said.
IPC officials on Wednesday further clarified the timing of the disposal.
K.K. Teo, executive director of IPC, told reporters that at the time the company announced its interim results the disposal exercise was still underway and was completed in December 1996.
"It was contractually agreed between the group and the purchasers...that they will have benefit of the results of the disposed subsidiaries for the whole of 1996," Teo said.
As such, the effective date became January 1, 1996.
"It was perhaps an oversight which then confused people," Teo said, in reference to the company not making clear the adjustment in its 1996 results.

"The group is very concerned that statements have been made that the group presented accounts that were misleading. Therefore it's very important for us to get this clear so that minority shareholders don't have the impression that we
presented a false set of accounts," Teo said.
He gave a further breakdown of IPC's extraordinary loss item of S$37.43 million, saying the group incurred losses of S$7.5 million in the sale of the disposed units.
A further provision of S$1.5 million was made for its investment in Zenith Data Systems Pte Ltd.
The group also incurred transfer costs of S$4.7 million when it transferred its point-of-sale business in the United Kingdom to a distributor.

Company officials said IPC had changed its business model, having taken the decision to streamline and dispose or reduce stakes in unprofitable units in the United States, Australia, Holland and Hong Kong.
They had decided instead to appoint distributors in those regions to sell its products to reduce risk.
Teo added that IPC was extending into the original equipment manufacturing business for its computer related products, making use of its facilities in China.
He told reporters he was unsure whether the company would undergo further re-structuring.

IPC previously said it made a provision of S$45.5 million for its exposure to its financially troubled South Korean unit and made a S$21.8 million extraordinary gain from sale of its investment in France's Groupe Bull.
On IPC's business strategy, Teo said the group had moved significantly into the manufacturing and sale of telecommunications equipment.
"The focus of the group will be along these lines because of the convergence of computer technology and telecommunications," he said.
-- Singapore newsroom (65-8703080)
